Citi's candidates (c_2024_1_D054, c_2024_1_D029) address disclosure controls and procedures and CECL transition provisions, which are unrelated to the EU Artificial Intelligence Act topic.

comparisons.peer_summary: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (E.U. AI Act) became effective in 2024, establishing rules for AI systems in the EU, with certain provisions applying from February 2025 and others between August 2025 and August 2027.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs explicitly identify the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) as a specific regulatory development effective in 2024 with phased-in application dates starting in February 2025. While JPMorgan broadly states the Act regulates the development and deployment of AI systems within the EU, Goldman Sachs provides more specific detail on the timeline, noting that certain provisions apply from February 2025 while others apply between August 2025 and August 2027, and that the Act establishes rules for placing AI systems on the market and putting them into service.

sentences.text: In addition, the EU Artificial Intelligence Act regulates the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems within the EU, with phased-in requirements that began in February 2025.
In addition, in 2024, the E.U. Artificial Intelligence Act (E.U. AI Act) became effective.
Certain provisions of the E.U. AI Act apply from February 2025, with other provisions applying between August 2025 and August 2027.
The E.U. AI Act establishes rules for placing on the market, putting into service, and using artificial intelligence systems in the E.U.
